recipes.name: Peanut Butter Fudge with Marshmallow Creme

steps.text: Line a 9x13 inch pan with foil or parchment paper.

Combine sugar, evaporated milk, and butter In a medium saucepan. Cook over medium heat stirring frequently until it comes to a boil. Boil for 10 minutes, remove from heat and stir in peanut butter and marshmallow creme.
Pour into the prepared pan and chill until set. Cut into squares and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Peanut Butter Fudge with Marshmallow Creme

review.reviewBody: Easy to make. Wonderful peanut butter flavor without overpowering, but not sickening sweet!! Doesn't get hard and crystalize like a lot of fudge does. Will definitely make this again.

This is the fudge recipe that I have made for over twenty five years. I have always doubled this amount so that it would make thicker pieces and serve a crowd plus have enough extra for my peanut butter lovers! I used an extra 2-1/4c of brown sugar and 2 1/2 c. white sugar, 1/2c. extra peanut butter, 1c. +1 Tbs. of salted butter, and 2 tsp. Of vanilla. These are the amounts for my DOUBLED RECIPE. This fudge NEVER has had a piece thrown out!!! It’s been a regular in our family. My late sister-in-law added the extra peanut butter and changed the recipe by using half white and half brown sugar, causing the fudge to have better flavor. However, the fudge didn’t harden quite as well. I adjusted the amount of sugars and butter, and added the vanilla. We BOILED IT FOR EXACTLY 8 MINUTES! Our family LOVES this fudge, especially at Christmas when it’s now also being requested by two new generations of peanut butter fudge fanatics! This recipe is from the ORIGINAL FANTASY PEANUT BUTTER FUDGE RECIPE. with our family’s tweaks. I so appreciate the Kraft family’s sharing those two FANTASY FUDGE recipes! Not only are the recipes reliable, but they produce a creamy and delicious fudge with much less effort! As I am aging, I appreciate those recipes with not only delicious results, but also ease of preparation with time honored flavors! This will be passed to generation of our family’s tweaks!

I made a few little adjustments to the recipe and it turned out awesomex10. When I read ingredients I thought that maybe there might just be a little too much sugar so I only put 3 1/3 c of sugar and then I added a little coffee cream, about 3 tbsp. Boiled it for 10 minutes but kept a close eye on it and tested it in cold water to see if it was forming a soft ball. Did not find it grainy, it was smooth and I also drizzled some 85% cocoa lindt chocolate on top. Sprayed a glass baking pan with cooking spray and was able to cut fudge out of it with ease. Thank you Teresa for the recipe and my famiy thanks you as well. Totally delicious!!!

This came out great! I did it a bit differently than the recipe tho. I used 1/2 white and 1/2 brown sugar, and I added the marshmallow along with the sugar, butter and milk to cook together. I think it makes the fudge smoother. Also, I always cook to the soft ball stage when making fudge like my Nana taught me. Time and candy thermometers aren't as reliable. Delicious flavor!!! I will make it again!

My phone sent my review before I finished, so look for rest below. I changed a few things but not the ingredients. I let it boil for 11 mins instead of ten minutes. I turn the burner down to the lowest temperature possible. I then add Peanut Butter and Marshmallow. Stir till it's all blended then turn off stove and pour into dish. If you turn it off right away it cools down too fast and it breaks while cutting it. I use a glass dish instead of metal. I spray the whole inside with cooking spray. The sliced pieces are prettier & fudge cools more evenly. After pouring in dish. I put plastic wrap over it set it in refrigerator till it's cold. Take out & let it warm to room temp. Turn over onto cutting board then give it a good thump and it pops right out. Gently turn over, cut and store in cool place. I like my fudge firm yet soft like fudge is suppose to be. My dad has no teeth and he has no problem eatting it because it breaks off easily & melts in your mouth. Enjoy.
My family has had this recipe since I was a child. You need to boil it for 8 minutes exactly and it will be perfect!! I am 70 and have used this recipe for 50 yrs now.

AMAZING!!! I did change it up just a tad. I used 1 7oz jar of marshmallow crème, and used salted butter instead of margarine. I also boiled for 7 minutes. I might try 8 minutes this time. I just made it on Sunday and here we are Tuesday night and I'm making a second batch. Thank you!!!

I have made this several times and the only 2 pieces of advice I can give is make sure you get evaporated milk instead of sweetened condensed milk and be sure to boil for 10 minutes not any less for the sugar to caramelize.
I used unsalted butter and everything else exactly. It was super- 😋- tasty! Thanks for this quick recipe...

I started with adding an entire can of evaporated milk (oops it's 12 oz) and I quickly started doing the math. I added 1 cup of brown sugar for a richer flavor, 1 Tbl of Peanut butter added and no additional ingredients. I am waiting for the results of my improvisational fix.
Very easy and very good. I only let it boil for 8 min. And it turned out perfect.
I love this recipe, I have made it several times and the family loves it
I made this yesterday, and it is absolutely delicious! Definitely a keeper.
This recipe is so good alot of sugar but yummy and pretty easy!!!!👍👍.

I've made this recipe several times for friends and family and they loved it. It's simple and easy and tastes like you spent hours preparing. It will melt in your mouth! It's a must try!!! Making it again tonight!
Fantastic recipe! Very easy and delicious to make.
Mine came out a bit hard. Still delicious though.
I give it 3 stars but mine came out like soup! I'm not sure what I did wrong, I will have to try it again!
